content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sentiment spikes (high sentiment values > 0.7), leading to overshoots.
- After a sharp price spike, model often fails to correct downward quickly — underestimates subsequent decline, especially when sentiment cools (sentiment < 0.5).
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model holds prices too high for too long after peaks, ignoring sentiment-driven pullback signals.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish (0.5–0.7), but fails to adjust when sentiment turns bearish (below 0.4).
- Model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts — e.g., when sentiment drops from 0.9 to 0.3, price drop is not fully captured in 3–5 day lag.
- Overshoots are more common after high sentiment days (e.g., sentiment > 0.8) — model overweights sentiment as bullish signal, leading to inflated forecasts.
- When sentiment is low (below 0.4) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — fails to recognize bottoming or reversal, leading to delayed downward bias.
